q: Halogens ($F_2$, $Cl_2$, $Br_2$, $I_2$) are ____ molecules.
e: Halogens (F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) are diatomic molecules. Diatomic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a ____ and iodine is a solid at room temperature.
e: Fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a liquid and iodine is a solid at room temperature. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They are ____ elements.
e: They are electronegative elements. Electronegative is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Since essential electronic structure of halogen is ____, they are very reactive.
e: Since essential electronic structure of halogen is ns2 np5, they are very reactive. Ns2 np5 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Among them ____ is the most reactive.
e: Among them fluorine is the most reactive. Fluorine is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Thus, none of the halogens can be found in nature in their ____.
e: Thus, none of the halogens can be found in nature in their elemental forms. Elemental forms is the idea that completes this fact.

q: They are found as salts of the ____.
e: They are found as salts of the halides. Halides is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with ____ and concentrated sulphuric acid.
e: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated sulphuric acid. Manganese(IV) oxide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine is prepared from the mixture of ____, manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated sulphuric acid on heating.
e: Chlorine is prepared from the mixture of sodium chloride, manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated sulphuric acid on heating. Sodium chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It is collected by the ____ because it is slightly soluble in water and heavier than air.
e: It is collected by the upward displacement of air because it is slightly soluble in water and heavier than air. Upward displacement of air is the idea that completes this fact.

q: If required dry, the gas is passed into ____.
e: If required dry, the gas is passed into concentrated sulphuric acid. Concentrated sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fluorine is a very ____ gas.
e: Fluorine is a very pale yellow gas. Pale yellow is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It is the ____ halogen and exists as a highly toxic gas.
e: It is the lightest halogen and exists as a highly toxic gas. Lightest is the idea that completes this fact.

q: As it is the most electronegative element, it is ____.
e: As it is the most electronegative element, it is extremely reactive. Extremely reactive is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It reacts with almost all other elements, except ____.
e: It reacts with almost all other elements, except helium and neon. Helium and neon is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine is a ____ gas with a choking, unpleasant smell.
e: Chlorine is a pale green gas with a choking, unpleasant smell. Pale green is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine is very ____ if inhaled even in small quantities.
e: Chlorine is very poisonous if inhaled even in small quantities. Poisonous is the idea that completes this fact.

q: One part of chlorine in ____ parts of air may be harmful.
e: One part of chlorine in 50,000 parts of air may be harmful. 50,000 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine is a heavy, ____, volatile liquid.
e: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, volatile liquid. Reddish brown is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It has a ____, irritating smell.
e: It has a choking, irritating smell. Choking is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine means '____'.
e: Bromine means 'a stench'. A stench is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Liquid bromine causes ____ on the flesh, which heal with difficulty.
e: Liquid bromine causes burns on the flesh, which heal with difficulty. Burns is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine is slightly soluble in water, forming a ____ solution containing about 3 percent of bromine at ordinary temperature.
e: Bromine is slightly soluble in water, forming a yellowish red solution containing about 3 percent of bromine at ordinary temperature. Yellowish red is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine is a ____ and irritating smell.
e: Iodine is a purple-black shiny solid and irritating smell. Purple-black shiny solid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine ____ rapidly when heated, forming a violet vapour from which the black solid can again be obtained by cooling.
e: Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a violet vapour from which the black solid can again be obtained by cooling. Sublimes is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine is almost insoluble in water but readily dissolves in ____.
e: Iodine is almost insoluble in water but readily dissolves in aqueous potassium iodide. Aqueous potassium iodide is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This is due to the formation of a compound of potassium iodide and iodine, which is ____.
e: This is due to the formation of a compound of potassium iodide and iodine, which is very soluble. Very soluble is the idea that completes this fact.

q: This solution is ____.
e: This solution is brown. Brown is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine also dissolves in ethanol and ether, forming brown solutions, and in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride, forming ____ solutions.
e: Iodine also dissolves in ethanol and ether, forming brown solutions, and in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride, forming violet solutions. Violet is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of ____.
e: Reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2. F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2 is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Halogens react with most compounds containing ____.
e: Halogens react with most compounds containing hydrogen. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab.

q: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to ____, it explodes.
e: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to sunlight, it explodes. Sunlight is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine combines with hydrogen, but ____ as chlorine does.
e: Bromine combines with hydrogen, but not as readily as chlorine does. Not as readily is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A mixture of bromine and hydrogen needs ____ to make them combine.
e: A mixture of bromine and hydrogen needs heat to make them combine. Heat is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine has ____ for hydrogen.
e: Iodine has little affinity for hydrogen. Little affinity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine reacts ____ with metals to form metal chlorides.
e: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form metal chlorides. Vigorously is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When a very thin sheet of an alloy of copper and zinc, mainly copper, is dropped into a chlorine gas jar, it burns brightly with a ____.
e: When a very thin sheet of an alloy of copper and zinc, mainly copper, is dropped into a chlorine gas jar, it burns brightly with a green flame. Green flame is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine combines ____ with most metals to form bromides.
e: Bromine combines readily with most metals to form bromides. Readily is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine is fairly active and will combine with many metals to form iodides, but it does so, ____ than either chlorine or bromine.
e: Iodine is fairly active and will combine with many metals to form iodides, but it does so, much less readily than either chlorine or bromine. Much less readily is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Phosphorus burns ____ in chlorine.
e: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine. Spontaneously is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine explodes when mixed with ____.
e: Bromine explodes when mixed with yellow phosphorus. Yellow phosphorus is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have ____, however, iodine does not.
e: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have bleaching power, however, iodine does not. Bleaching power is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine reacts with water to form ____ and $HCl$.
e: Chlorine reacts with water to form HOCl and HCl. HOCl is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The $HOCl$ slowly decomposes to ____.
e: The HOCl slowly decomposes to nascent oxygen. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal.

q: This process is speeded up by ____.
e: This process is speeded up by light. Light is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by ____ them.
e: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by oxidising them. Oxidising is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine will bleach ____.
e: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. Moist litmus papers is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine is also used as a bleaching agent but it is ____ as chlorine.
e: Bromine is also used as a bleaching agent but it is not as effective as chlorine. Not as effective is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Halogens are ____.
e: Halogens are oxidising agents. Oxidising agents is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into ____.
e: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into iron(III) chloride. Iron(III) chloride is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine is also an oxidising agent, but it is ____ an oxidising agent as chlorine.
e: Bromine is also an oxidising agent, but it is not as strong an oxidising agent as chlorine. Not as strong is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine is a ____ oxidising agent, but it will not perform many of the ordinary oxidising actions attributed to chlorine and bromine.
e: Iodine is a mild oxidising agent, but it will not perform many of the ordinary oxidising actions attributed to chlorine and bromine. Mild is the idea that completes this fact.

q: However, iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and ____.
e: However, iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and liberate sulphur. Liberate sulphur is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Halogens also react with ____.
e: Halogens also react with alkalis. An alkali is a soluble base that produces OH- ions in water.

q: When chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide or sodium iodide, the respective halogen is ____ by more reactive chlorine.
e: When chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide or sodium iodide, the respective halogen is displaced by more reactive chlorine. Displaced is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When bromine is passed into a solution of sodium iodide, iodine is ____.
e: When bromine is passed into a solution of sodium iodide, iodine is liberated. Liberated is the idea that completes this fact.

q: However, iodine cannot ____ chlorine and bromine from their salt solutions.
e: However, iodine cannot displace chlorine and bromine from their salt solutions. Displace is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a ____.
e: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a negative charge. Negative charge is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The halide anions are fluoride ($F^-$), chloride ($Cl^-$), bromide ($Br^-$) and ____.
e: The halide anions are fluoride (F-), chloride (Cl-), bromide (Br-) and iodide (I-). Iodide (I-) is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding ____.
e: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding silver nitrate solution. Acidified silver nitrate is a test for chloride: a white precipitate of AgCl appears. A solution is a homogeneous mixture of solute dissolved in solvent.

q: Samples are typically acidified with ____ to remove interfering ions, e.g. carbonate ions.
e: Samples are typically acidified with dilute nitric acid to remove interfering ions, e.g. carbonate ions. Dilute nitric acid is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Different colours of ____ precipitates are observed.
e: Different colours of silver halides precipitates are observed. Silver halides is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Fluorine is used in the form of fluorides in drinking water to ____ by hardening the enamel on teeth.
e: Fluorine is used in the form of fluorides in drinking water to prevent tooth decay by hardening the enamel on teeth. Prevent tooth decay is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Chlorine is used to make ____ (Polyvinyl chloride) plastic as well as household bleaches.
e: Chlorine is used to make PVC (Polyvinyl chloride) plastic as well as household bleaches. PVC is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It is also used to kill ____ in drinking water.
e: It is also used to kill bacteria and viruses in drinking water. Bacteria and viruses is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and ____.
e: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and fire retardants. Fire retardants is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Iodine is used in medicines (e.g., to treat cases of ____) and disinfectants (due to its antiseptic properties, e.g. 'Tincture of iodine') and also as a photographic chemical.
e: Iodine is used in medicines (e.g., to treat cases of goiter) and disinfectants (due to its antiseptic properties, e.g. 'Tincture of iodine') and also as a photographic chemical. Goiter is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Halides are used in the ____.
e: Halides are used in the solder paste. Solder paste is the idea that completes this fact.

q: It is widely used in metal halide lamps that are ____.
e: It is widely used in metal halide lamps that are high-intensity discharge lamps. High-intensity discharge lamps is the idea that completes this fact.
